Disability services, Eastern Suburbs, Sydney

Disability Services in Sydney's Eastern Suburbs for High Support Needs

For people with high physical support needs, especially in the months after a spinal injury.

The Eastern Suburbs are home to the Prince of Wales Hospital and its spinal injury unit, so many people in the east live with high physical support needs. Abundance Healthcare Group provides nurse-led care at home for them: bowel and bladder routines, skin care, transfers and repositioning, with every plan written by a registered nurse.

  1. Home
  2. Locations
  3. Sydney
  4. Eastern Suburbs

What it is

High support needs care in the Eastern Suburbs

We provide care at home in the Eastern Suburbs for people with high physical support needs, such as tetraplegia, paraplegia or advanced neurological conditions. That includes bowel and bladder routines, pressure care, transfers, repositioning and the nursing tasks that go with them, all to plans a registered nurse has written.

Disability services in the Eastern Suburbs of Sydney are plentiful for everyday support, but fewer take on high intensity routines. As an NDIS provider for the Eastern Suburbs, from Randwick and Maroubra to Bondi, we are based in Campbelltown, which affects lead times, as explained below. The overview of disability services across Sydney shows every region.

What we deliver

Supports for people with high physical needs in the east

In the east we provide high intensity daily personal activities, community nursing, daily personal care, and community access and transport. For people with high physical needs, the four usually come together: clinical routines morning and evening, nursing visits for catheters and skin, and help to get out.

High intensity daily personal activities

Bowel care, catheter care and, where needed, PEG feeds, carried out by workers trained on the participant's own plan and signed off by the nurse.

Community nursing at home

A registered nurse handles suprapubic catheter changes, pressure injury care and reviews, and checks that the daily routine is protecting the skin.

Daily personal care

Hoist transfers, showering, dressing and meals. Repositioning during the day follows the plan's schedule, and changes in skin are reported the same shift.

Community access and transport

The beaches and coastal walks, Randwick and Bondi Junction, university, work and appointments, with a worker who drives a wheelchair accessible vehicle where one is booked.

Local support

After the Prince of Wales spinal unit

The Prince of Wales Hospital at Randwick has a spinal injury unit within the South Eastern Sydney health district. Leaving it means moving from a ward with nurses on hand to a home where trained workers carry the routine. The months that follow are when plans are tested hardest.

We start before discharge: a nurse reviews the bowel, bladder and skin plans with the unit, checks the home equipment and trains workers on the participant's own routine. Our page on spinal cord injury NDIS support covers the first months at home. For ward staff, our page on hospital to home support explains the process. The hospital is named for geography, and we have no formal arrangement with it.

What it is

Ready to go home? What needs to be in place

For someone with high physical needs, going home safely depends on equipment, trained people and written plans being ready before the discharge date. The checklist sets out what needs to be in place and who usually arranges it. Anything left open is worth raising with us early.

ItemWho arranges it
Pressure care mattress and cushion deliveredHospital occupational therapist, with the NDIA for funding
Ceiling or mobile hoist installed and checkedOccupational therapist and the equipment supplier
Bowel care plan written for homeOur nurse, from the spinal unit's plan
Bladder plan and catheter supplies at homeOur nurse and the participant or family
Autonomic dysreflexia emergency planThe treating team, briefed to every worker by our nurse
Workers trained on transfers and routinesOur nurse
Overnight repositioning, if neededAgreed in the roster, confirmed case by case
Follow-up clinic datesThe spinal unit

Funding

NDIS funding for high support needs

High support needs are funded mainly from Core Supports: high intensity personal care, daily personal care and nursing as a disability-related health support. Equipment and home modifications come from Capital Supports. We claim within the NDIA's pricing schedule and list every item in the service agreement.

Early plans after a spinal injury sometimes underestimate the hours needed. The nurse's notes from the first weeks at home are good evidence for a plan change, and we provide them to the coordinator with consent.

Timing

Capacity in the east

The east is one of the furthest parts of Sydney from our Campbelltown office, so capacity is checked carefully. We reply within one business day. Nursing visits are booked on set days; a full roster depends on finding trained workers who live within reach of the home.

  1. Refer. Discharge planners, coordinators and families can refer with the supports and the dates.
  2. Capacity. We confirm which workers and nurse days are available.
  3. Pre-discharge planning. The nurse reviews the plans and the home.
  4. Day one at home. Where notice allows, signed-off workers and a booked nursing visit are in place for the first day after discharge.

Who delivers it

Clinical oversight

A registered nurse oversees each participant's care. The nurse writes the plans, signs off each worker on each task, reviews skin, bowel and bladder routines on a schedule and after any hospital admission, and is the person workers call when something looks wrong.

We are a registered NDIS provider, Registration ID 4-JCLD6XE. High intensity tasks follow the NDIS Commission's skills descriptors. Incidents are recorded and reviewed, and complaints can be made to us or to the Commission.

Local support

Recent support in the Eastern Suburbs

Support in eastern suburbs homes and along the coast, photographed with the participant's written agreement. We keep faces, number plates and recognisable buildings out of every picture we publish.

Where we work

Randwick, Maroubra, Bondi and surrounds

We take referrals from the Randwick, Waverley and Woollahra council areas: Randwick, Kensington, Kingsford, Coogee, Clovelly, Maroubra, Matraville, Malabar, Bondi, Bondi Junction, Bronte, Waverley, Dover Heights and Paddington. Availability depends on where trained workers live.

West of the city, we also support people in the Inner West.

Common questions

Eastern Suburbs questions

Can you set up care before discharge from Prince of Wales?

Yes, given notice. A nurse reviews the spinal unit's plans, checks the home equipment and trains workers on the participant's routine before the discharge date. Tell us the date as early as possible.

Do you cover Bondi and Coogee?

Yes. Bondi is in the Waverley council area and Coogee in Randwick, and both are inside our service area. We confirm which trained workers live within reach before accepting a referral.

Do you provide overnight turns?

Overnight repositioning is confirmed case by case. It needs trained workers living close to the home for each night of the roster. We tell you within one business day whether we can staff it.

Do workers have spinal injury training?

Workers are trained by our nurse on the participant's own plans: bowel care, bladder care, transfers, skin checks and the emergency plan for autonomic dysreflexia. Each is signed off before working alone.

Is capacity limited in the east?

Yes, more than in the south west. The east is a long way from our Campbelltown office, so we depend on finding workers who live nearby. We say plainly what we can cover before you commit.

Can you work with my private therapists?

Yes. With your consent, our nurse shares the plans with your physiotherapist, occupational therapist or exercise physiologist and builds their recommendations into what workers do each day.

High support needs in the Eastern Suburbs?

If a discharge from Randwick is coming up, give us the date and the care plan. You will have an answer within one business day.

Ask about the east

Tell us the suburb, the discharge date if there is one, and the supports needed. We reply within one business day.

Registered NDIS provider, Reg ID 4-JCLD6XE.

At a glance

  • Randwick, Waverley and Woollahra councils
  • Bowel, bladder and skin routines to written plans
  • Planning starts before discharge
  • Enquiries answered within one business day
